name: Brian Eno
description:
'''Brian Eno''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|iː|n|oʊ}} {{Respell|EE|no}}; born '''Brian Peter George Eno''', 15 May 1948) is an English musician, [[record producer]] and artist. He is known for his pioneering contributions to [[ambient music|ambient]], [[Electronic music|electronic]] and [[generative music]], and for producing, recording, and writing works in [[rock music|rock]] and [[pop music]]. He describes himself as a "non-musician" uninterested in [[virtuosity]], and advocates for [[Recording studio as an instrument|using the studio as a compositional tool]]. He has been described as one of popular music's most influential and innovative figures.

Eno was born in [[Melton, Suffolk]], and studied at [[Ipswich School of Art]] and the [[Winchester School of Art]]. He joined the [[glam rock]] band Roxy Music in 1971, contributing to their first two albums, and left in 1973. In 1974, Eno released his first solo albums, ''[[Here Come the Warm Jets]]'' and ''[[Taking Tiger Mountain (By Strategy)]]''. His third, ''[[Another Green World]]'' (1975), combined rock with [[Minimal music|minimal]] instrumental tracks. Eno coined the term "ambient music" to describe music he conceived to be "as ignorable as possible", and released a string of albums in the genre, including ''[[Ambient 1: Music for Airports]]'' (1979). 

Eno's profile rose when he contributed to the [[David Bowie]] albums ''[[Low (David Bowie album)|Low]]'' (1977), ''[["Heroes" (album)|Heroes]]'' (1977) and ''[[Lodger (album)|Lodger]]'' (1979), known as the [[Berlin Trilogy]], and produced the [[Talking Heads]] albums ''[[More Songs About Buildings and Food]]'' (1978), ''[[Fear of Music]]'' (1979) and ''[[Remain in Light]]'' (1980). With [[Daniel Lanois]], Eno produced the [[U2]] albums ''[[The Unforgettable Fire]]'' (1984), ''[[The Joshua Tree]]'' (1987) — one of the [[List of best-selling albums|highest-selling albums in history]] — and ''[[Achtung Baby]]'' (1991). Eno produced [[Coldplay]]'s album ''[[Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends]]'', the highest-selling album of 2008, and co-wrote their next album, ''[[Mylo Xyloto]]'' (2011). He has also produced albums by [[Ultravox]], [[Devo]], [[Harold Budd]], [[Laraaji]], [[James (band)|James]], [[Laurie Anderson]] and [[Paul Simon]], and released albums with artists including [[Robert Fripp]], [[David Byrne]], [[Jon Hassell]], [[Cluster (band)|Cluster]], [[Roger Eno]], [[John Cale]], [[Karl Hyde]], [[Jon Hopkins]] and [[Fred Again]]. Eno composed [[Microsoft Sound|the startup music]] for [[Windows 95]] and has scored films including ''[[The Lovely Bones (film)|The Lovely Bones]]'' (2009). His visual art includes ''[[77 Million Paintings]]'', a [[generative art]] installation first exhibited in 2006.

[[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|''Rolling Stone'''s 2023 list of the 500 greatest albums]] includes two Eno albums, plus albums he created with Roxy Music, Bowie, Devo, Talking Heads and U2''.'' In 2019, Eno was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] as a member of Roxy Music. He is an activist on behalf of [[humanitarian]], [[Environmentalism|environmental]], [[anti-war]] and [[pro-Palestinian]] causes and is a founding member of the [[Long Now Foundation]].
